full_judgment: 2. It is the case of the writ petitioner that the retail vegetable vendors have formed the petitioner samity and have been carrying on business in the Middle Circular Read within A.G.B. Colony, Dhaka since 1965. The Dhaka City Corporation constructed 82 shops and handed over possession to the members of the petitioner's samity. Thereafter, towards December, 1997 the Corporation invited tender for allotment of the shops. Pursuant to a writ petition filed by the petitioner the High Court Division disposed of the same with certain Observations and thereafter, it also filed another writ petition in which the High Court Division issued a rule and directed to maintain status-quo. The petitioner samity also instituted another suit seeking declaration that the Corporation has no power to allot the shops other than to the members of the petitioner samity. The suit was decreed but the decree was ultimately set aside by the lower appellate court, against which, a civil revision is pending before the High Court Division. One Ashachhal Muktijoddah Poribar Kallyan Bahumukhi Samabaya Samity Ltd. filed a writ petition over the said shops which was also disposed of by the High Court Division with a direction upon the Corporation to dispose of their application in accordance with law. Subsequently, the Corporation illegally issued notices upon the members of the petitioner to vacate the shops in favour of the Corporation which compelled it to file writ petition. Respondent Nos. 1-4 filed two separate affidavits-in-opposition denying the averments made in the writ petition and claimed that the writ petitioner has no locus standi to file the writ petition and that the members of the samity being temporary allottees of the shop premises, they have acquired no right to continue as allotees under the Corporation and therefore, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the impugned judgment discharged the rule.
